item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"After Tshisekedi’s coalition won the December 2023 legislative elections, formation of the government was delayed amid negotiations over National Assembly leadership appointments.","question_ids":["8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns post-election developments originating in 2023, but the reported delay and institutional consequences extend into 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the delayed government formation and related appointment process to Tshisekedi’s coalition and presidential administration.","limitations":["The source is a 2024 retrospective and does not provide exact duration, budgetary effects, or implementation outcomes during 2023.","The evidence concerns government formation rather than completed policy delivery."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi’s coalition won the December 2023 legislative elections, while several major coalition figures were elected to Parliament rather than appointed to the subsequent government.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.8","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly fits the December 2023 legislative-election period, although the appointment consequence was reported in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the coalition’s legislative victory and the allocation of political figures between Parliament and government to Tshisekedi’s political leadership.","limitations":["The source does not independently assess the fairness of the elections or whether opposition victories were accepted.","It does not establish the extent of parliamentary independence or effective checks in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa as Prime Minister, making her the first woman to head the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and formed a government of 54 ministers.","question_ids":["4B.7","8B.2","8B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The appointment followed the December 2023 election but was announced five months into Tshisekedi’s second term in 2024, so it has limited direct fit to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the appointment of Suminwa and the cabinet composition to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The appointment occurred in 2024, outside the target year.","The source provides no evidence about Suminwa’s performance, qualifications, or service outcomes during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The new government contained 55% first-time ministers, including first-time appointees in interior, defence, and foreign-affairs portfolios; many appointees came from Tshisekedi’s UDPS party.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This describes the government announced in 2024 after the 2023 election and therefore is only indirectly relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the composition and party orientation of the cabinet to Tshisekedi’s appointment choices.","limitations":["The source does not assess the appointees’ competence, independence, resources, or performance.","The cabinet composition was not in force during most or all of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The source characterizes Tshisekedi’s appointment strategy as using UDPS loyalists and technocrats to insulate ministers from political dynamics and promote a more fluid government operation.","question_ids":["4B.5","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This is an analyst’s interpretation of the 2024 cabinet, with roots in the post-December 2023 political transition rather than evidence confined to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source explicitly presents the strategy as Tshisekedi’s objective and decision.","limitations":["This is an analytical characterization, not a documented performance measure.","The source does not show whether loyalty or technical expertise actually improved coordination or implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi’s party-reflective government was described as breaking with the post-conflict practice of allocating ministerial posts through coalition compromise, while the constitution retained a semi-presidential structure with parliamentary checks.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","8B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The described break occurred in the government formed after the December 2023 elections and was reported in 2024; it is relevant to the transition from the 2023 electoral period.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the shift away from coalition compromise to Tshisekedi’s decision to form a government reflecting his party.","limitations":["The source does not establish that constitutional rules were violated.","It does not measure the practical extent of parliamentary checks or party capture during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The source identifies a risk that Tshisekedi’s presidentialist approach could concentrate power despite constitutional parliamentary checks, and notes that representatives from Maniema Province objected to their exclusion from the government.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.7","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The concern relates to the post-December 2023 government formation and its anticipated consequences, with reporting in 2024 rather than evidence limited to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the presidentialist approach and government composition to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["This records an identified risk and regional objection, not a demonstrated completed outcome.","The source does not quantify exclusion or show whether remedies were offered."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ba2345d010d20b","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"As of the report’s 2024 assessment, armed groups continued to control territory in eastern DRC, including an expansion of M23’s hold in North Kivu, while the administration confronted violence involving armed groups and neighbouring countries.","question_ids":["2B.10","3B.6","3B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The conflict conditions were ongoing after 2023 and provide context for Tshisekedi’s second-term environment, but the unit does not give a 2023-specific measurement.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the continuing challenge to the Tshisekedi administration’s security environment, while identifying M23 and neighbouring countries as external or non-state actors.","limitations":["The source does not establish Tshisekedi’s direct responsibility for M23’s territorial expansion.","No casualty, displacement, budget, or territorial-control figures are provided for 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The document is published in 2024 and primarily evaluates government formation after the December 2023 elections; evidence directly confined to calendar year 2023 is limited.","The source is an analytical article rather than a primary government record, audit, court finding, or independently verified dataset.","No material facts were identified for most nuclear-risk, integrity, economic-wellbeing, or social-wellbeing lenses."]}
